endorsements.quote: Second, when medical AI systems trained on synthetic data are used to inform diagnosis, prognosis, or treatment decisions, patients should consent to receiving care influenced by these tools.
First, individuals whose real data is used to train synthetic data generation algorithms should consent to this use.

unlisted_practices: Conduct research into the extent of bias in AI-generated synthetic data and methods for addressing it before implementing these techniques in healthcare.
Do not rush to adopt AI-generated synthetic data without adequate safeguards, particularly given potential harm to underserved populations.
Address structural barriers that prevent genuine inclusion of underserved populations in medical research rather than pursuing synthetic data solutions.
Establish validation frameworks and sensitivity analyses for AI-generated synthetic data.
Obtain input from underserved populations when creating data intended to represent them.
Inform patients when medical AI recommendations are based partly or entirely on artificially generated data rather than real patients.

screen.reason: This is a conceptual/ethical perspective and commentary article discussing the limitations and ethical concerns of using AI-generated synthetic data for underserved populations in healthcare.
